newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks drop two percent in nervous trading.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks drop two percent in nervous trading.

text.p: Swiss shares slumped two percent on Thursday as U.S. economic data, the weaker opening on Wall Street, the sagging dollar and remarks by Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan put pressure on stocks, dealers said.
Dealers said the market remained nervous and may ease more ahead of the Fed's policy-setting FOMC meeting on March 25.
"But I don't think we will fall below 4,200 points in the SMI any time soon," one dealer said. He added the general outlook was largely positive given investors' lack of alternatives to shares.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) fell 92.2 points, or 2.03 percent, to 4,442.9 points. The day's low was at 4,432.7, the high at 4,532.6.
The all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) slipped 50.84 points, or 1.77 percent, to 2,828.66.

One dealer said Greenspan's remarks were interpreted as a signal that the Fed was going to push up U.S. interest rates. He added a rate hike of a quarter percentage point was already discounted in prices.

Roche certificates slid 100 francs to 11,900 but kept losses in check after temporarily rising earlier in the session. Dealers said a CSFB study saying the group could set up a stock buy-back programme buoyed its shares.
Novartis registered shares led the actives list, sliding 41 francs to 1,708. Ciba Specialty Chemicals eased 3.50 francs to 112.25.
Insurer Winterthur was the only winner in the blue-chip segment. Its shares added six francs to 976.

Among banks, Credit Suisse Group lost 4.50 francs to 161.75 and UBS bearers shed 39 francs to 1,254. VP Bank bearer shares added 30 francs to 1,850 after the Liechtenstein-based bank reported a strong rise in 1996 group net.
Alusuisse, which had seen strong demand on Wednesday, slumped 40 francs to 1,202.
